answer_text:
Let

\[
H_n=\sum_{k=1}^n \frac1k.
\]

We want

\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{H_n}{\binom{n+100}{100}}.
\]

First interchange the order of summation:

\[
S=\sum_{n=1}^\infty \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{1}{k}\cdot \frac{1}{\binom{n+100}{100}}
=\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac1k \sum_{n=k}^\infty \frac{1}{\binom{n+100}{100}}.
\]

Now we evaluate the inner tail. For \(n\ge 1\),

\[
\frac{1}{\binom{n+99}{99}}-\frac{1}{\binom{n+100}{99}}
=
\frac{99!n!}{(n+99)!}-\frac{99!(n+1)!}{(n+100)!}.
\]

Putting over a common denominator,

\[
=\frac{99!n!}{(n+100)!}\bigl((n+100)-(n+1)\bigr)
=\frac{99\cdot 99!n!}{(n+100)!}.
\]

But

\[
\frac{1}{\binom{n+100}{100}}
=\frac{100!n!}{(n+100)!}
=\frac{100}{99}\cdot \frac{99\cdot 99!n!}{(n+100)!}.
\]

Thus

\[
\frac{1}{\binom{n+100}{100}}
=
\frac{100}{99}
\left(
\frac{1}{\binom{n+99}{99}}-\frac{1}{\binom{n+100}{99}}
\right).
\]

This telescopes, so

\[
\sum_{n=k}^\infty \frac{1}{\binom{n+100}{100}}
=
\frac{100}{99}\cdot \frac{1}{\binom{k+99}{99}}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S=\frac{100}{99}\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{k\binom{k+99}{99}}.
\]

Now use the Beta integral. For \(k\ge 1\),

\[
\frac{1}{k\binom{k+99}{99}}
=
\frac{99!(k-1)!}{(k+99)!}
=
\int_0^1 x^{k-1}(1-x)^{99}\,dx.
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{k\binom{k+99}{99}}
=
\int_0^1 (1-x)^{99}\sum_{k=1}^\infty x^{k-1}\,dx.
\]

For \(0\le x<1\),

\[
\sum_{k=1}^\infty x^{k-1}=\frac1{1-x},
\]

so

\[
\sum_{k=1}^\infty \frac{1}{k\binom{k+99}{99}}
=
\int_0^1 (1-x)^{98}\,dx
=
\frac1{99}.
\]

Thus

\[
S=\frac{100}{99}\cdot \frac1{99}
=
\frac{100}{9801}.
\]

So \(p=100\) and \(q=9801\), giving

\[
p+q=100+9801=9901.
\]

\[
\boxed{9901}
\]
